title: Reference-derived VCF Automation multi-step change with accurate failure reporting
prompt:
Implement the change runner in src/VcfaChangeClient.java. It is a dependency-free, single-file Java client for the VCF Automation 9.1 REST API in a VM Apps tenant org; runChange and the six per-operation helpers below it are stubbed and have to be written. VCF Automation publishes no OpenAPI specification, so docs/contract.json - transcribed from the Broadcom xAPIs reference pages listed in docs/official_sources.json - is the wire authority, and nothing it does not name may be called.

runChange performs one change, in order: exchange the refresh token for an access token; create the project; request the catalog item into the project it just created; poll that deployment until it reports a terminal status; submit the day-2 action against it; poll the resulting request until that reports a terminal status. Every call after the token exchange carries the access token as an Authorization: Bearer credential.

Honour the contract's wire rules exactly. The token exchange is form-encoded and percent-encodes its values. JSON bodies serialize their fields in the order the contract documents. An optional field the caller left unset - null, an empty string, an empty list, an empty map - is omitted from the request rather than sent as null, "", [], {} or an invented default; that applies to the nested zoneAssignmentConfigurations limits and to optional query parameters too, so an operation whose optional query parameters are all unset is sent with no query string at all. Fields documented as integers go on the wire as JSON numbers. A poll carries no request body and no Content-Type. Poll at the contract's interval and attempt limit and stop as soon as a terminal status is observed.

Then report what actually happened. A day-2 request that fails does so with HTTP 200 and status FAILED, so a 2xx response never establishes that the requested change succeeded. The returned ChangeReport must carry one StepOutcome per attempted step, in execution order, using the STEP_* names and the SUCCEEDED/FAILED vocabulary; a step the appliance accepted stays SUCCEEDED even when a later step fails; outcome is FAILED with failedStep naming the first step that did not succeed; failedRequestId and failureDetail carry the failed request's identifier and the server's own details text verbatim, not paraphrased or summarised. persistedChanges lists, in the order they were made, every change that still exists on the appliance after the run: the kind ("project" or "deployment"), the identifier the appliance returned, and the state the appliance last reported for it, or "CREATED" for an operation that reports no state. The contract exposes no operation that undoes an earlier step, so do not attempt a rollback and do not call anything outside the contract.

Run python3 tests/verify.py. Only src/VcfaChangeClient.java is an implementation file, it must stay a single Java source file, and it must not take on third-party dependencies; docs/ and tests/ are protected fixtures and must not be changed.
